from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('pages',len(reader.pages))
texts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(reader.pages):
 t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 texts.append(f'\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(texts))
print('\\n'.join(texts[:3]))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from itertools import product
for placement in [(0,1),(1,0)]:
 P=[[int(s==placement[u]) for s in range(2)] for u in range(2)]
 witnesses=[]
 for z in product((0,1), repeat=4):
  Z=[list(z[:2]),list(z[2:])]
  ok=all(Z[v][i]>=P[v][i] for v in range(2) for i in range(2))
  ok=ok and all(Z[1][i]<=Z[0][i] for i in range(2))
  ok=ok and all(Z[1][i]<=P[1][i]-P[0][i]+1 for i in range(2))
  if ok: witnesses.append(Z)
 o=P[0][0]*P[1][1]*10
 objective=2+o+max(1,o)
 print({'stages_one_based':tuple(v+1 for v in placement),'satisfies_Eq6':bool(witnesses),'Z_witness':witnesses[0] if witnesses else None,'Eq4_communication_cost':o,'Eq2_objective_for_c2':objective})
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
scratch=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for page in range(1,28):
 (scratch/f'page-{page:02d}.png').unlink(missing_ok=True)
(scratch/'manuscript.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
scratch.rmdir()
Path('tmp').rmdir()
print('Removed temporary extraction and rendering files; manuscript preserved.')
PY"

strengths: UniAP addresses an important practical problem: selecting pipeline partitions and per-layer DP, TP, and FSDP strategies under communication and memory constraints. This is relevant to efficient training of large vision transformers.

Table 1 reports meaningful measured improvements. On EnvB, ViT-Huge reaches 45.58 samples/s versus 38.74 for Alpa and 32.20 for Galvatron; Swin-Huge improves from 13.90 to 19.08 samples/s over Galvatron. The Llama-7B result achieves the reported 3.80× throughput improvement.

The evaluation spans several hardware environments and reaches 32 DCUs. Appendix G shows UniAP matching the best throughput found by an exhaustive Megatron configuration sweep for both Llama sizes, supporting practical usefulness even where throughput does not exceed the baseline.

The modular workflow, hardware descriptions, strategy visualizations, and solver settings help explain the system. The reported average throughput-estimation error of 3.59%, compared with Galvatron’s 11.17%, provides useful initial evidence for the cost model.
weaknesses: The central formulation admits incorrectly costed pipeline assignments. Equations (6a–c) enforce contiguity within each stage, but do not enforce stage order along graph edges. For a two-layer chain u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies the placement and contiguity constraints, yet Equation (4) charges zero cross-stage communication. Appendix B proves contiguity only and does not resolve this issue. This can change the optimizer’s preferred solution and is a material correctness concern.

The stated GPipe memory model appears incomplete. Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size b=B/c into CostModeling, while Section 3.2 computes activation memory from that batch size and Equation (5) has no explicit dependence on c. With activation checkpointing disabled, GPipe retains activations from multiple micro-batches before backward execution. The manuscript does not explain how this accumulated memory is represented, leaving its claimed memory-feasibility guarantee unsupported.

The repeated optimality claims exceed the evidence. Appendix E permits termination after 15 seconds with a gap below 4% and imposes a 60-second limit, without reporting achieved optimality certificates. Section 3.5 treats this time limit as constant; that bounds the search budget, not the time required to obtain an optimum. Moreover, estimation accuracy is evaluated only on selected strategies, which does not establish correct ranking across candidates. These issues, together with the formulation concerns, outweigh the useful empirical results.

The ablation does not isolate the contribution of joint optimization over hierarchical optimization. Table 2 compares against inter-only and intra-only variants, whereas the main competing approaches already combine both categories. For ViT and Swin, the inter-only variant even matches full UniAP. A hierarchical decomposition need not itself lose optimality; a comparison using matched candidate strategies, costs, and execution would be needed to support the paper’s causal explanation.

The optimization-time results have limited scope. UniAP’s reported time measures UOP and excludes initial profiling. Appendix G compares this against executing an exhaustive collection of Megatron training configurations. These results demonstrate savings over the specified procedures, but do not establish equivalent end-to-end startup savings or isolate algorithmic efficiency from implementation and resource differences.

There is also a correctable but significant specification gap: Equations (3) and (4) contain quartic products of placement and strategy variables, so the written formulation is not directly an MIQP. An auxiliary-variable reformulation is possible but is not described. Reproducibility remains partial because the checklist describes supplying only the solver component, while profiling, cost construction, and execution are essential to reproducing the system results.
